relations.note: Jupiter governed daytime lightning, while Summanus governed nighttime lightning.
Both received sacrifice when officials could not determine whether lightning struck by day or night.
Summanus’ terracotta image reportedly stood upon the Capitoline temple of Jupiter.

relations.myth: Jupiter supersedes Summanus in public honor
relations.note: Jupiter allegedly drew worshippers from formerly prominent Summanus after receiving a grander temple.
Late-antique interpretation made Summanus another name for the underworld ruler Pluto.
Summanus emerged from the earth in a quadriga, seized Proserpina, and carried her underground.
Dumézil structurally opposed bright, juridical Dius Fidius to dark Summanus; no ancient interaction is attested.
Dumézil comparatively associated Summanus’ dark sovereignty with Varuṇa; ancient sources never equate them.
